Here's the handoff. Lead item: **the log ends at 03:59 with the gateway still failing and no rollback recorded in `deploys.csv` — assume this is live and unmitigated.**

# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** ACTIVE / UNMITIGATED as of last data at `2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z`
**Severity:** Customer-facing. 83% of production API traffic failing on the affected node.
**Prepared:** 2026-08-28 · from `logs/gateway.log`, `logs/worker.log`, `deploys.csv`

## TL;DR

A gateway config change flipped connection pooling to one-connection-per-request. The 20-connection pool saturated 33 seconds later and has never recovered. Roll back gateway config generation 119 → 118.

## Root cause

Config generation 119, applied at `02:13:41.234Z`, set:

```
gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true
```

This makes each in-flight request hold its own pool connection instead of sharing. With `size=20`, concurrency above 20 cannot be served at all — excess requests queue, exceed the acquire deadline, and return 503.

The failure mode is `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`, raised **before** the gateway ever contacts an upstream. There are exactly two error messages in the file, emitted as a matched pair on the same request id, 530 of each:

```
ERROR access  req-N /v1/<route> -> <svc> 503 <N>ms
ERROR pool    req-N ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)
```

Not an upstream fault. There is no upstream error, timeout, or connection failure anywhere in the log.

## Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **Onset** | `2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z` (first 503, `req-07401`); first `acquire slow` WARN 4s earlier at `02:14:14.920Z` |
| **End** | None — errors continuous to end of data at `03:59:27.974Z` |
| **Duration** | ≥ **1h 45m**, ongoing |
| **Error rate** | 530 of 1228 requests (43% overall); steady **83%** from 02:2x onward |
| **Detected** | `03:21:05.282Z` — on-call paged at 71% 5m error rate, **67 min after onset** |

**Affected:** `/v1/cart`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/session` — 106 failures each, evenly distributed across all four upstreams (accounts, billing, catalog, orders).

**Not affected:** `/v1/profile` (slow acquires only, no 503s) and `/health`.

**Not self-recovering.** The wait queue grows monotonically with no plateau — the pool has been at `in_use=20 idle=0` on every sample since 02:15, with `waiting` climbing ~20 every 5 minutes to 172 and still rising at last sample. It will not drain on its own.

## Roll back: dep-4471

```
dep-4471  gateway  2026-03-14T02:12:00Z → 02:14:00Z  a.novak
          "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"
```

**Action: revert gateway config generation 119 → 118.**

Be aware generation 119 carried three keys. A full generation rollback also reverts the second one:

| key | 118 | 119 | implicated? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gateway.pool.perRequest` | false | **true** | **yes — this is the cause** |
| `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` | 2000 | 2500 | no |
| `gateway.log.sampleRate` | 1.0 | 1.0 | no-op |

During an active incident I'd take the **full rollback to 118** — it's the known-good state and the fastest path. The `upstreamMs` bump reverting alongside is acceptable collateral; re-land it separately. If someone specifically needs the 2500ms timeout retained, revert only `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` instead.

**Verify recovery** on the `pool stats` lines (emitted every 5 min): `idle` should return above 0 and `waiting` to 0. Pre-incident baseline was `in_use` oscillating 3–11, `idle` never below 9, `waiting=0`. 503 rate should go to zero within one sample interval.

**Do not** simply raise `pool.size` as the fix. That raises the concurrency ceiling but leaves per-request pinning in place; it will re-saturate under load.

## Timeline

```
02:12:00   dep-4471 starts
02:12:12   config reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119
02:13:41   generation 119 applied, perRequest false -> true
02:14:00   dep-4471 reports FINISHED — pipeline recorded a clean deploy
02:14:14   first  WARN pool acquire slow: waited 100ms          (+33s from apply)
02:14:18   first ERROR 503 / ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED                 (+37s from apply)
02:15:58   pool pinned: in_use=20 idle=0 waiting=12
03:21:05   on-call paged, error_rate 5m avg 71%
03:55:58   pool still pinned: in_use=20 idle=0 waiting=172
03:59:27   last log line — still failing
```

Note the deploy was marked **successful at 02:14:00, 19 seconds before the first 503**. The pipeline shows green; don't let that rule it out.

## Ruled out

- **Upstream services** — zero upstream errors; failures are uniform across all four upstreams (~132–133 each) and all five routes (106 each). Consistent with a bottleneck in front of them, not any one of them.
- **Database / shared backend** — `worker.log` covers the identical window with **0 errors** and **1080/1080 jobs succeeded**. Worker DB pool is byte-identical on all 18 samples (`size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0`), including across 02:14. Workers hit the same DB and show nothing.
- **dep-4469** (accounts-svc rate limit on `/v1/session`) — tempting since `/v1/session` fails, but it fails at exactly the same count as the other four routes, and a rate limit returns 429, not 503.
- **dep-4468, dep-4470** — both finished before the log's clean 74-minute window (01:00–02:14, `waiting=0` throughout).
- **dep-4472, dep-4473** — both landed *after* onset. Flagged below as triage hazards.

## Watch out — two red herrings

`dep-4473` (catalog-svc, cache ttl 60s→300s) started at **03:20, one minute before the 03:21 page**. Anyone paged at 03:21 who opens `deploys.csv` sees a catalog-svc deploy in progress at that exact moment. It is 66 minutes downstream of the real onset. `dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41) is likewise after the fact.

## Open items after rollback

1. **Scope check — other nodes.** The log header reads `node-3 of 3`. I only have this one node's log. Config generations are usually fleet-wide, so assume nodes 1 and 2 are also affected until confirmed. **Verify before declaring resolved.**
2. **`/health` is blind to this.** 180/180 health checks returned 200 throughout, because health checks don't go through the connection pool. The load balancer had no reason to eject the node while 83% of real traffic failed. Health check should exercise the pool.
3. **67-minute detection gap.** Paging fired on a 5-minute average error rate. `waiting > 0` on the pool, or the first `acquire slow` WARN, would have fired within a minute.
4. **Separate issue — worker slowdown.** Job durations ramp linearly 200ms → 2324ms (11.6×) across the three hours, uniform across all six job types, **with no inflection at 02:14** — unrelated to this incident and already in progress at the log's first line. `db_wait` stays ≤12ms, so it is not DB contention. Zero job failures, so lower urgency, but worth a ticket. `dep-4470` (worker, 00:48) is the timing suspect; worker.log starts at 01:00 so there's no pre-deploy baseline to confirm it. Pull logs from before 00:48 to settle it.

## Data caveats

Sub-minute timestamps are out of order within each burst (e.g. `03:39:59.650` followed by `03:39:03.922`, which should be 03:40), and the per-request `waiting N` counter in the error lines resets periodically — it climbs to 271 then drops back to ~12. Use the 5-minute `pool stats` lines for the queue trend; they're consistent. Neither issue affects the onset time or the root cause.
